newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends on lingering demand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends on lingering demand.

text.p: Taiwan's overnight interbank rate ended higher on Wednesday, buoyed by minor but persistent demand for cash in the run-up to Friday's Chinese lunar new year, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.718 percent against Tuesday's 6.583 close, with 30-day commercial paper holding stable at 6.00-6.25 percent.
The central bank injected T$7.885 billion in funds into the banking system on Wednesday.
Dealers said many banks stopped borrowing, thinking that the rate would rise in the last trading day as the market closes for the five-day holiday beginning Thursday.
They said they expected money rates to fall after the holidays as funds would start to return to the banking system.
The bond market was quiet with investors stepping to the sidelines before the holidays.
The money and bond markets will close on Thursday and reopen on Tuesday.
